context_heading: What to understand about breast augmentation and finding a local surgeon
context: Breast augmentation uses implants or fat transfer to increase breast size or improve shape. In the UK, cosmetic surgery should be carried out by a surgeon on the GMC's specialist register, usually in plastic surgery or a related specialty, in a hospital or clinic registered with the CQC (or the equivalent regulator outside England). Many surgeons are members of BAAPS or BAPRAS, and the Royal College of Surgeons offers a cosmetic surgery certification.

The GMC requires doctors offering cosmetic interventions to give patients time to reflect before agreeing to surgery, and not to use high-pressure sales. Your consultation should be with the surgeon who will operate, so you can ask questions and make an informed choice.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say that you are looking for breast augmentation and give your location so we can introduce you to a suitable local professional.
Mention whether you are interested in implants, fat transfer, or would like to discuss both options.
Explain what you hope to achieve, such as increased size or improved shape, so the surgeon can prepare for your consultation.
Let us know if you have any relevant medical history or previous breast surgery, as this may affect your options.
Say whether you have a preference for a particular type of clinic or hospital setting, if you have one.
Include any questions you already have, so the professional can address them when they quote.
questions: Are you on the GMC's specialist register, and in which specialty?
Is the hospital or clinic where you operate registered with the CQC or the equivalent regulator?
What are the risks and complications of breast augmentation, and how are they managed?
Will my implant details be recorded on the Breast and Cosmetic Implant Registry?
How should I choose between implants and fat transfer, and what are the trade-offs?
What aftercare and follow-up do you provide, and what happens if I have concerns later?

faqs.q: How do I check that a cosmetic surgeon is properly qualified for breast augmentation?
faqs.a: You can check that the surgeon is on the GMC's specialist register, usually in plastic surgery or a related specialty. It is also worth confirming that the hospital or clinic is registered with the CQC or the equivalent regulator in your nation.

faqs.q: Will my implant details be recorded somewhere?
faqs.a: Yes, implant details go on the Breast and Cosmetic Implant Registry, which helps trace implants if needed. You can ask your surgeon to confirm this.

faqs.q: Do I need to choose the implant size at the first consultation?
faqs.a: No, you should discuss size realistically and take time to reflect before deciding. The GMC requires doctors to give you time to reflect and not to use high-pressure sales.

faqs.q: What should I expect at a consultation for breast augmentation?
faqs.a: Your consultation should be with the surgeon who will operate, and you should have the opportunity to ask questions and discuss your goals. You should not feel pressured to book surgery on the day.
